terms.gloss: reject, turn down (an offer, a plan, advice)
evidence: Plaut. Trin. 455: quī condiciōnem hanc repudiēs?
Caes. B.G. 1.40 (Lewis & Short): grātiam populī Rōmānī repudiāre
terms.comment: The usual word for turning down something offered: an offer of marriage or terms (condiciōnem), a favour, a plan. Its first sense is to divorce or cast off a spouse or a betrothed (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Rep. 1.16 (Lewis & Short): Sōcratem omnem istam disputātiōnem rejēcisse
terms.comment: Literally to throw back (a cloak over the shoulder, a weapon at the enemy), so to push away, rule out, or spurn a suitor (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 3.99 (Lewis & Short): gustātus id quod valdē dulce est aspernātur
terms.comment: Rejection with aversion, the opposite of appetere; very frequent in Cicero (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: Satin' tū es sānus mentis aut animī tuī, quī condiciōnem hanc repudiēs?
phrases.english: Are you in your right mind, turning down an offer like this?
I’m dropping the plan I first had in mind.

phrases.latin: An id est sapere, ut quī beneficium ā benevolente repudiēs?
phrases.english: Is that being wise, to turn down a kindness from someone who means you well?

sources: Lewis & Short: repudio · Lewis & Short: reicio · Lewis & Short: aspernor
Plaut. Trin. 454–455, 637, Ter. And. 733 and Phorm. 717 checked against the Perseus Latin texts (11 November 2026).
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, p. 362.
